Waluipedia cast sheet — Mario. Built by tools/build-character-sheets.py, hand-authored from the article. XP ledger: level 5, power rating 14 → a level 5 Monk player-character sheet for 955 BF (Mario at his height; never above the ledger level — a past self holds no more experience than the present one). The year Peach died. Before Highsun 1 the hero was always near her, and the routine still held: Bowser kidnaps Peach, Mario stomps through eight worlds, Peach bakes a cake.. Numbers are a GM-ready reading of the record, not a filed stat line; the article stays the authority. Archive date 1040 BF.

The Plumber Who Vanished — Mushroom Kingdom (Former Hero) / Unknown

Status: Missing — Presumed alive, location unknown, last confirmed sighting 1039 BF at the Star Fountain

Mario is—or WAS—the most famous hero in the Mushroom Kingdom. The man who saved Princess Peach countless times before her assassination in 955 BF. The red-capped plumber who could jump higher than physics should allow, who stomped Bowser's schemes into the ground repeatedly, who was so synonymous with heroism that his NAME became a verb. And then, after eighty-five years of diminished appearances and growing silence, he DISAPPEARED entirely. Luigi found him at the Star Fountain. They flew together on wing caps. Luigi said 'Nothing can hurt us... as long as we're together.' And then Mario was GONE again, and Luigi is working alone for the Mages' Guild at Raventree Manor, sucking up ghosts with a vacuum cleaner and refusing to explain ANYTHING. Waluigi has spent considerable effort piecing together what happened. The picture that emerges is worse than a simple disappearance. WAH. The Garden Above the Fire does not return Mario; it makes his absence louder, because Luigi's rescue ends with Luigi asking the brother who is not in the room whether they are still superstars.

description.value: Monk — the class this sheet reads the record as. Levels follow the XP ledger.
Folk Hero — the life the article describes before the table.
A leaping stomp from above. If Mario moved at least 10 feet straight toward the target first, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Strength save or be knocked prone.

A bouncing fireball thrown from the palm (range 60/120 ft.). On a hit the target also catches alight for 1d4 fire damage at the start of its next turn unless it or another creature uses an action to put it out.
Mario's long jump is 30 feet and his high jump 20 feet, with or without a running start. He can jump as part of his movement and takes no damage from falls of 60 feet or less.
Mario makes two Stomp attacks, or one Stomp and one Fire Flower attack.
As a bonus action Mario eats a Super Mushroom: he regains 2d10 + 5 hit points and is Large until the end of his next turn, with advantage on Strength checks and saves while he is.
Mario ignores the first level of exhaustion he would gain each day, and a short rest restores him as a long rest would once per day. (The 1040 BF sheet replaces this with Diminished.)

When a creature Mario can see attacks Princess Peach or an ally within 5 feet of him, Mario can use his reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll; if it still hits, he can take the damage instead.

Toads and Mushroom Kingdom citizens who can see Mario have advantage on saving throws against being frightened. Once per long rest, as an action, he rallies: up to six allies within 30 feet gain temporary hit points equal to his level plus his Charisma modifier.
Mario cannot willingly abandon an innocent in danger he can see. He has advantage on saving throws against effects that would make him flee or stand aside.
